per_finding.id: author note: git-core helper push is completion
per_finding.notes: tests/hooks/test-shell-analysis-gates.sh:85-86 now expects COMPLETION BLOCKED for '/usr/lib/git-core/git-push origin HEAD'; the test passes (claude, in the coverage run). Right behaviour: the allowlist only parses argv of a program named git, a direct helper call is rare and not provably a feature push, and DECISIONS F2 says the strictest tier for unseen code.

issues.problem: HEAD, @ and a bare push are resolved against the branch checked out when the hook runs, not after the earlier segments of the same command. A command that switches to the default branch first and then pushes HEAD is classified as a feature push.
issues.evidence: p8.sh on feat/x with planning floor: 'git checkout main && git push origin HEAD', 'git switch main && git push', 'git checkout -q main; git push origin @', 'git stash; git checkout main; git push -u origin HEAD', 'git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main && git push origin HEAD' -> 'Intermediate commit allowed' (claude and codex exec_command). Real run of 'git checkout -q main && git push origin HEAD': remote main 33d9a74..47ea660.
issues.suggested_fix: If any earlier command in the analysis can change HEAD (git checkout/switch/symbolic-ref/update-ref HEAD/stash/rebase/worktree, or any opaque segment), treat HEAD/@/bare pushes as completion; only resolve HEAD from the hook's checkout when nothing before the push can move it. Add test rows.

issues.problem: A push whose working directory the analysis could not resolve (cwd null) is placed in the hook's own cwd: '$c.cwd' null becomes '' in @tsv, and 'cd ""' then pwd -P returns the hook cwd. A cd inside a function body is not tracked either. The documented rule ('unresolved directories are completion') does not hold.
issues.evidence: p5/p6.sh: 'cd "$(cat dirfile)" && git push origin HEAD', 'cd "$(head -1 dirfile)" && git push', 'read D < dirfile; cd "$D" && git push origin HEAD', 'D=$(cat dirfile); cd $D; git push', 'cd "$OLDPWD" && git push', 'cd "$D" && git push', 'f(){ cd <main worktree>; }; f; git push origin HEAD' -> intermediate (dirfile holds the main worktree path). Real run of the function form: remote main 174071b..33d9a74.
issues.suggested_fix: Return 1 when a push command's cwd is null/empty (emit a sentinel instead of an empty TSV field), and have the analyzer mark cwd unknown after calling a shell function that runs cd (or after any function call). Add rows for each form.

issues.problem: The destination is read from argv only. Git config changes what a push sends: remote.<name>.push maps an explicit 'git push origin feat/x' (and bare pushes) to another ref, push.default=upstream/matching pushes the upstream or every matching branch, push.followTags pushes tags, remote.<name>.mirror mirrors. Both stored config (set by an earlier, ungated 'git config') and inline 'git -c' are accepted ('-c' is skipped without being judged).
issues.evidence: p2/p10.sh: stored remote.origin.push=refs/heads/feat/x:refs/heads/main then 'git push origin feat/x' -> intermediate, real push 'feat/x -> main' (359430d..330bebe); push.default=upstream with upstream origin/main, 'git push' -> intermediate, real 'feat/x -> main'; push.default=matching, 'git push' -> intermediate, real 'main -> main'; 'git -c push.followTags=true push origin feat/x' -> intermediate, real '* [new tag] v7.0'; stored push.followTags=true -> intermediate; 'git -c remote.origin.push=...:refs/heads/main push origin feat/x', 'git -c push.default=matching push', 'git -c remote.origin.mirror=true push origin feat/x' -> intermediate.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat any 'git -c' on a push as completion (or allow only a short list of harmless keys), and before allowing, read the target repo's config: remote.<remote>.push, remote.<remote>.mirror, push.default (allow only unset/simple/current) and push.followTags must be unset/false, else completion. Add tests with stored and inline config.

issues.problem: Destinations are checked against LOCAL refs and origin's default only. Git resolves an unqualified destination against the REMOTE's refs, so a local branch named 'heads/main' or named like a remote tag passes; and the default of any remote other than origin (or a URL remote) is never consulted.
issues.evidence: p3.sh: with local branch heads/main, 'git push origin feat/x:heads/main' -> intermediate, real push 'feat/x -> main' (remote main 4e42840..28a3c6e); with a local branch rtag and remote tag rtag, 'git push origin +feat/x:rtag' -> intermediate, real '+ feat/x -> rtag (forced update)' moves the remote TAG; second remote up with HEAD -> develop: 'git push up develop', 'git push up feat/x:develop', 'git push <url>/up.git develop' -> intermediate.
issues.suggested_fix: Require every destination to be written as, or resolve to, refs/heads/<name> where <name> contains no 'heads/' / 'tags/' / 'remotes/' prefix component; reject (completion) unqualified destinations that match a remote-tracking tag or that the remote may resolve differently (or simply require refs/heads/ qualification for anything ambiguous). Compute default names for the remote actually pushed to (refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD, and completion for URL remotes or remotes without a known HEAD).

issues.problem: The default-branch names come from the local checkout ($PWD), but the MCP write targets tool_input.owner/repo, which may be any repository. A write to another repository's default branch (e.g. 'develop') passes as a feature write.
issues.evidence: p9.sh: push_files / create_or_update_file / delete_file / create_commit with owner o, repo r, branch 'feat/nonexist' (stand-in for another repo's default 'develop') -> 'Intermediate commit allowed'; code reads only ca_default_branch_names "$PWD".
issues.suggested_fix: Allow intermediate only when owner/repo match the local origin remote (parse remote.origin.url) and the branch is non-default there; otherwise completion. Add a test row.

issues.problem: The release commit is still taken from the wrong place for valid gh spellings: (a) '-p/--preview NAME' is missing from apivals, so the endpoint is misread and the releases call is not found; (b) a command that creates two releases (gh release create + gh api releases, or two gh release create) checks only the first; (c) repeated target_commitish fields take the first while gh sends the last.
issues.evidence: prel.sh (origin/main=OM green, RED=597e2ad): 'gh api -p corsair repos/o/r/releases -f target_commitish=RED' -> OM; '--preview corsair' -> OM; 'gh release create v9 --target main && gh api repos/o/r/releases -f tag_name=v10 -f target_commitish=RED' -> OM; 'gh release create v9 --target main && gh release create v10 --target RED' -> OM; 'gh api repos/o/r/releases -f target_commitish=main -f target_commitish=RED' -> OM. Also 'repos/o/r/releases/' (trailing slash) -> OM (if GitHub accepts it).
issues.suggested_fix: Add -p/--preview to apivals; count ALL release creations (gh release create commands + releases API calls + MCP) and deny 'cannot determine release commit' when there is more than one; deny when target_commitish/tag_name appears more than once; accept an optional trailing slash in the endpoint regex.

issues.problem: Over-gating of an honest flow: a branch created in the same command does not exist when the hook runs, so the new-branch push is final delivery.
issues.evidence: p8.sh: 'git checkout -b feat/n && git push -u origin feat/n' -> COMPLETION BLOCKED (planning floor met). 'git switch -c feat/n && git push -u origin HEAD' -> intermediate (but only because HEAD is resolved to the pre-command branch, see issue 1).
issues.suggested_fix: Accept a destination created by an earlier 'git checkout -b/switch -c/branch NAME' in the same analysis (and resolve HEAD to it), once issue 1 is fixed.
